column3: “Began” is not separately expressed in the Greek imperfect.
BSB has “a city,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the article (“the city,” τὴν).
In the critical text “many” (πολλοὶ) of those having unclean spirits is the subject of “were coming out”; BSB makes the spirits the subject.
“His words” supplies an object where the Greek says they heeded him; “divine power” renders “power of God.”
The Greek names signs before great mighty works; BSB applies “great” to both.
“The Holy Spirit” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
“Peter and John” makes the unnamed subject explicit.
“Our ministry” specifies the Greek “this matter” or word.
BSB makes forgiveness a separate possible action by the Lord; the Greek asks whether the intent may be forgiven.
BSB interprets the images of being in bitter gall and a bond of injustice as “poisoned” and “captive.”
“Peter and John” supplies the unnamed subject.
The Greek leaves “this is deserted” as a separate statement; BSB attaches it directly to the road.
“On his way he met” supplies a verb where the Greek introduces the man with “behold.”
“The man” and the repeated “Philip” make Greek referents explicit.
